 Judgment
1. These appeals are filed by the insurer challenging the liability imposed on it by the Tribunal.

2. It was the case of the insurer that in the Medico- Legal Case register, it had been recorded as accident between the school bus and auto-rikshaw, whereas in the claim petitions, it was merely stated that the driver of the auto-rikshaw had lost control and as a result, the auto- rikshaw toppled,
resulting in injuries to the claimants.
It is, therefore, contended that in the light of these contradictory pleas regarding the accident, it was clear that the insurer could not be made liable if a school bus was involved.

The Manager vs Marakka on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15040946/
4 3.

It was also contended that the offending auto- rikshaw, which was insured by the appellant, did not have the permit to ply on the road where the accident occurred and therefore, on this ground also, the insurer is also not liable.
4. As far as the contention of the insurer that the Medico-Legal Case Register contained an entry regarding the accident between the auto-rikshaw and a school bus is concerned, the insurer has not chosen to examine the author of the entries in the Medico-Legal Case Register.

In the absence of any evidence from the person who made the entries in the Medico-Legal Case Register, the argument of the learned counsel for the insurer that the entries in the Register are to be accepted, cannot be sustained and this argument is therefore rejected.

5. Another contention raised by the learned counsel for the insurer that the offending auto-rikshaw did not possess the requisite permit is concerned, it has to be stated here that this is essentially a contention that there was a breach of policy conditions.

If there is breach of policy conditions, the only remedy available for the insurer would be to pay the compensation to the claimants and thereafter proceed to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
6. In this view of the matter, there is no merit in these appeals and the appeals are dismissed.
7. However, it is made clear that the insurer can proceed to recover the compensation amount after it deposits the same before the Tribunal, from the owner of the offending vehicle.
8. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.

Sd/-
